**Best fit: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its **2,600 W inverter** can handle a single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, with more headroom than an 1,800 W station, and its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives you useful cooking capacity. At full power, expect roughly **about an hour of continuous cooking** after conversion losses; real meals often use less because the burner isn’t always running at full power. ([Specs and runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

It should also suit an electric kettle **as long as the kettle’s rated wattage is under 2,600 W**. As a rough guide, the cited estimate is around **90–110 Wh to boil a litre**, so the battery can provide multiple boils. Check the wattage on your cooktop or kettle before buying, and remember that using both appliances at once adds their wattages together.
